channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbek-Turkish cooperation reaches new heights in tourism sector
item.description: Tourism between Uzbekistan and Turkey has seen dynamic growth, with bilateral agreements and increased tourist exchanges. The number of Turkish tourists to Uzbekistan nearly doubled in two years, reaching 149,146 in 2024. Uzbekistan also saw a 17.4% increase in its citizens visiting Turkey in 2025. This success aligns with Uzbekistan's overall tourism boom, positioning it among states with high international tourism growth rates.

item.title: UN Rapporteur Warns Against Granting Legitimacy to Taliban Without Rights Improvements
item.description: UN Special Rapporteur Richard Bennett cautioned that international engagement with the Taliban should not legitimize their rule without verifiable improvements in human rights. He noted that repression and discrimination in Afghanistan have become increasingly entrenched since the Taliban's return to power five years ago.

item.title: Samarkand Summit Sets Global Priorities for Children's Wellbeing
item.description: A London Post article highlights the Samarkand international summit on investing in children's wellbeing, emphasizing initiatives for child rights, dignified living conditions, and potential realization. The Samarkand Declaration reaffirms commitment to the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, focusing on protection from violence, digital safety, early development, inclusive education, and healthcare.

item.title: Tajikistan Hosts Conference on CIS Cooperation and Development Prospects
item.description: A conference on the development and strengthening of cooperation within the CIS was held in Dushanbe, Tajikistan. Participants discussed current issues of interaction, regional integration, and multilateral cooperation. The event was organized by the Institute for the Study of Asian and European States and included representatives from government bodies, diplomatic missions, and research institutions from Tajikistan and Russia.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan Expand Cooperation in Arts and Culture
item.description: Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan have signed a memorandum of cooperation between the State Institute of Arts and Culture of Uzbekistan and the Kazakh National Academy of Choreography in Tashkent. The agreement aims to foster academic exchange, share experiences, and strengthen ties between educational institutions. It includes student and faculty exchanges, joint projects, and the organization of conferences and masterclasses.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Phase Out Cash Payments on Electric Trains and Buses by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Transport has drafted a presidential resolution to gradually transition to cashless payments for passenger transport. The plan aims to eliminate cash transactions on suburban trains and intercity buses by January 1, 2030, with all payments made electronically. To encourage adoption, a temporary discount on electronic tickets is proposed for passengers.

item.title: Kazakh Citizen Sentenced in Russia for Illegal Immigrant Smuggling
item.description: A 43-year-old citizen of Kazakhstan, employed as a train driver by Russian Railways, has been sentenced to two years and five months in prison in Omsk, Russia. He was found guilty of organizing the illegal entry of a foreign national into the Russian Federation as part of a group. The court heard that he facilitated the border crossing for a fee of 100,000 rubles.

item.title: Uzbek President Arrives in Turkey for Turkic States Summit
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev of Uzbekistan has arrived in Ankara, Turkey, for a working visit at the invitation of President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan. He will participate in the upcoming summit of the Organization of Turkic States, focusing on strengthening multilateral cooperation. The summit is expected to adopt the Ankara Declaration and several agreements.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans Unified Digital Transport Platform for Seamless Travel
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to launch a unified national digital transport platform, "Bir yo‘l," by January 1, 2028. This platform will integrate rail, air, bus, and urban transport systems, allowing passengers to plan journeys door-to-door, book tickets, and make payments through a single system. The initiative aims to simplify travel and enhance passenger experience.

item.title: Central Asian Cultural Figures Honored with State Awards
item.description: Vice President Yerlan Karin presented state awards to prominent cultural and art figures from Central Asian countries in Akorda. The awards, including the 'Dostyk' Order of the II degree, recognized contributions to strengthening friendship and developing cultural ties.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches Pilot Project for Rural Development in Five Regions
item.description: Kazakhstan is launching a pilot project named 'Rural Development Team' in five regions to increase rural incomes and provide targeted support to families. The initiative focuses on personalized assistance for job searching, skill acquisition, and entrepreneurship.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Gas Production Faces Decline Despite New Wells
item.description: Uzbekneftgaz reports a decline in natural gas production from major fields due to depleted reserves, with new wells unable to compensate for the shortfall. The company plans to extract 22.8 billion cubic meters of gas by year-end, a decrease from 2025's projected 25.2 billion cubic meters. Depleted reserves, exceeding 80% in some fields, are the primary cause.

item.title: Pashto Language Discussed as Bridge for Kabul-Islamabad Reconciliation
item.description: A discussion titled 'Tahawol' explored the role of the Pashto language as a potential bridge for reconciliation between Kabul and Islamabad. The event highlighted the cultural and linguistic connections that could foster better relations between Afghanistan and Pakistan. Details were shared by Ariana News.

item.title: Uzbekistan Enhances Local Council Oversight Effectiveness Through Practical Seminar
item.description: A practical seminar was held in Uzbekistan for local councils, focusing on improving deputy oversight. Discussions covered effective use of deputy inquiries, enhancing the role of councils in addressing public appeals, and strengthening accountability of officials. Recommendations were developed to improve local council operations and deputy control.

item.title: New Stone Wool Production Plant Launched in Karaganda Region, Kazakhstan
item.description: A new stone wool production plant has been launched in the Saran industrial zone of the Karaganda region, Kazakhstan. The enterprise will produce up to 1.2 million cubic meters of thermal insulation material annually, supporting the 'People's Construction' program and reducing import dependence. The project involved 67 billion tenge in investment.

item.title: National Bank of Kyrgyzstan Warns of New 1% Interest Rate Scam
item.description: The National Bank of Kyrgyzstan has warned citizens about scammers using the regulator's name and distributing fake documents via messengers. Scammers pose as financial advisors, offer loans at 1% annual interest, and request personal data. The bank urges the public not to trust such documents or share sensitive information.

item.title: Taliban Announce Release of 252 Afghan Migrants from Pakistani Prisons
item.description: The Taliban announced that 252 Afghan migrants have been released from Pakistani prisons and returned to Afghanistan. The Ministry of Refugees and Repatriation stated that 15 individuals returned via Spin Boldak and 237 via Torkham crossing. Pakistan has recently intensified arrests and deportations of Afghan migrants.

item.title: Almaty Hosts Discussion on Developing Technological Infrastructure for Artificial Intelligence
item.description: The Freedom Talk discussion club in Almaty hosted "Freedom AI: Inside Infrastructure," focusing on the development of artificial intelligence and its technological infrastructure. Participants discussed the future of AI, modern data centers, technological partnerships, and the role of infrastructure in AI solutions.

item.title: Russia Intensifies Recruitment of Africans for Ukraine War, UN Investigators Report
item.description: UN investigators have concluded that Russia is intensifying efforts to recruit individuals from African countries for the war in Ukraine, allegedly deceiving or forcing citizens from 29 nations into military service. Meanwhile, Putin accused the West of exploiting Africa's natural resources and creating debt dependency.

item.title: EU: Taliban's Gender Discrimination May Constitute a Crime Against Humanity
item.description: The European Union has condemned human rights violations and institutionalized discrimination against women and girls in Afghanistan, stating that systematic violations could constitute gender persecution as a crime against humanity. The EU called for an immediate lifting of restrictions and urged the Taliban to halt executions and respect minority rights.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Receive Over 100 Million Euros for Climate-Resilient Landscapes
item.description: Uzbekistan will receive over 103.7 million euros from the Green Climate Fund for the regional 'Climate-Resilient Landscapes in Central Asia' (CLiCA) program. The funds will be used for restoring forests and pastures, introducing climate-resilient agricultural technologies, and reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey presidents sign agreement on high-level business support council
item.description: Uzbekistan President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Turkish President Rejep Tayyip Erdog‘an signed an agreement to establish a high-level council for business support following talks in Ankara. Several other bilateral documents were also signed.

item.title: Six Kazakh Wrestlers to Compete on Day Seven of World Championships in Astana
item.description: Six Kazakh wrestlers will compete on the seventh day of the World Wrestling Championships in Astana. Four freestyle wrestlers will have their initial bouts, while one will participate in a repechage match. Another wrestler will compete for a bronze medal in women's wrestling.

item.title: UN Rapporteur Urges Action Against Taliban's Repression and Discrimination
item.description: UN Special Rapporteur Richard Bennett called for preventing the normalization of the Taliban's repression and discrimination in Afghanistan. He stated that the Taliban have intensified human rights violations and decrees undermining women's rights. Bennett urged accountability for violations and continued humanitarian aid.

item.title: Georgia's ruling party moves to outlaw five major opposition parties
item.description: Georgia's ruling Georgian Dream party is initiating proceedings to ban five of the country's largest opposition parties. This move, which began hearings at the Constitutional Court on October 21, is seen as an authoritarian drift that could push a significant portion of the opposition out of the legal political sphere ahead of the 2028 parliamentary elections.

item.title: Industrial accident disrupts work at Tajikistan's Rogun Dam
item.description: An industrial incident occurred at Tajikistan's Rogun Dam on October 21, disrupting construction work. Conflicting reports suggest either no injuries or at least five workers were hurt. State officials claim no one was harmed, while RFE/RL reports, citing witnesses, indicate a more serious situation with workers trapped.

item.title: Woman Arrested for Asking Putin to Send Troops to Kazakhstan
item.description: A woman has been arrested in Uzbekistan for appealing to Russian President Vladimir Putin to send troops into Kazakhstan. She also reportedly insulted the citizens of Kazakhstan in her appeal, stating that "every Kazakh should recognize their master." The woman's actions are under investigation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan plans home delivery of license plates and car documents by 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to launch home delivery of state license plates and technical passports for vehicles starting December 1, 2026. The country also anticipates a 27% increase in regional electricity demand by 2030, requiring immediate preparation of capacities and networks to support new factories and growing cities.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Arrives for Turkic States Summit in Ankara
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived at the Kuliye palace complex in Ankara to attend the 13th summit of the Organization of Turkic States. He was welcomed by Turkish Vice President Cevdet Yılmaz. The summit is expected to focus on regional cooperation and development among member nations.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Build Nearly 70 Medical and 50 Social Facilities in Regions
item.description: Kazakhstan's Parliament Committee on Regional and Infrastructure Development discussed implementing the President's directive on modernizing infrastructure. The committee supports the initiative to declare the upcoming year a year of nationwide construction. Plans include building approximately 70 medical and 50 social facilities across the regions.

item.title: Uzbekistan Parliamentary Delegation Participates in Dushanbe International Forum
item.description: The Uzbekistan parliamentary delegation attended an international forum in Dushanbe. Senate Chairperson Tanzila Narbayeva proposed strengthening regional peace, expanding cooperation, and developing inter-parliamentary ties among Central Asian nations.

item.title: Central Asian Nations Agree on QR Payment System Integration by 2026
item.description: Central banks of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Azerbaijan have agreed to develop an integrated QR payment system by the end of 2026. This initiative will allow citizens to make payments abroad using their domestic mobile banking apps and transfer money in real-time.

item.title: CIS Agreement Ratified to Combat Evasion of Debt and Assets Abroad
item.description: Russia's Federation Council approved the ratification of a CIS agreement on data exchange for enforcing court decisions. This pact will simplify debt collection and make it harder for debtors to hide assets internationally by facilitating information sharing among member states.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey Presidents Discuss Strengthening Bilateral Relations
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Ankara. They discussed strengthening Uzbek-Turkish strategic partnership in political, economic, and cultural spheres. Key points included establishing a high-level Business Support Council and expanding cooperation on promising projects. The leaders also exchanged views on international and regional agendas.

item.title: Afghan UN Envoy Warns Taliban Policies Are Destroying a Generation's Future
item.description: Afghanistan's Chargé d’Affaires to the UN, Nasir Ahmad Faiq, stated that Taliban restrictions on women and girls, and deprivation of children's rights, are ruining the future for an entire generation. He highlighted that 3.8 million girls were denied education in 2024 and warned of profound consequences for Afghanistan.

item.title: Kazakhstan Woman Suspected of Forging Documents for Foreigners
item.description: In Ust-Kamenogorsk, Kazakhstan, a 28-year-old woman is suspected of forging three temporary residence permits for citizens of a neighboring country. The documents were not officially registered. Authorities are conducting a pre-trial investigation, and the woman is obligated to appear when summoned.

item.title: Staphylococcus and E. coli Found: Cause of Student Poisoning at Almaty Physics and Mathematics School Identified
item.description: An investigation at an Almaty physics and mathematics school revealed microbial contamination in some prepared foods, including E. coli bacteria in food samples and dish rinses. Disinfectant solutions also failed to meet standards. Four cafeteria workers tested positive for Staphylococcus aureus.

item.title: Pakistan and Afghanistan Armies Exchange Fire, Resulting in Casualties
item.description: New clashes between Pakistani and Afghan military personnel have led to casualties on both sides. Two people died and two were injured in eastern Afghanistan due to shelling from Pakistani territory. Pakistan's border service reported one death and five injuries in northwestern Pakistan from mortar shelling by Afghan troops.

item.title: Astana to Experience Temporary Heating, Hot Water, and Electricity Outages on October 30
item.description: Parts of Astana will face temporary disruptions to heating, hot water, and electricity on Friday, October 30. These shutdowns are due to scheduled repairs on the heating network, electrical work, and tree trimming. Specific addresses affected have been published.

item.title: New Multidisciplinary Medical Complex with Oncology Center to be Built in Almaty
item.description: A new multidisciplinary medical complex, including an oncology center, is planned for construction in Almaty. The project aims to enhance healthcare infrastructure in the city.
